home.title: Psychological support for children and families
home.intro: Sometimes, a child's behaviour is the visible part of emotions that are hard to express, developmental needs, or difficulties in their relationships. Together, we can better understand what lies behind these expressions and find support suited to the child, the parent, their relationship, and the whole family.
home.recognitionTitle: You may have come here because…
recognition: your child is going through a difficult time and you want to understand their experience better;
you notice emotional, behavioural, or relational changes that concern you;
your relationship with your child has become strained, or understanding each other feels harder;
your child finds it difficult to adjust to nursery, school, or other changes in their life;
tensions between siblings or other difficulties affect the balance of the whole family;
the challenges of parenting feel overwhelming and you need support to understand your child's needs and how to be there for them.

supports.title: Your child
supports.text: When you notice emotional, behavioural, relational, or adjustment difficulties and want to better understand the needs behind them.

supports.title: You, as a parent
supports.text: When you need support to understand your child's experience, respond to their needs, and feel more confident as a parent.

supports.title: Family relationships
supports.text: When tensions arise between parent and child, between siblings, or within the family, and you need support to understand them and build more balanced relationships.

supports.title: Online support for Romanians abroad
supports.text: Psychological support sessions in Romanian, held exclusively online, for children, parents, and families living outside Romania.

home.approachTitle: First, we understand. Then, we build together.
home.approachText: In my work, professional training and clinical experience meet a calm, authentic, and approachable presence. I want the people I work with to feel heard, respected, and understood, without judgement or pressure to find every answer immediately.
steps: Send an inquiry, even if you do not yet know which form of support is appropriate.
We discuss the request and clarify the child's and family's needs.
We agree on a next step when working together is appropriate.
home.resourcesIntro: Articles about child development, parenting, and family relationships.
home.closingTitle: You do not need to have every answer.
home.closingText: You can start with a question. Together, we can clarify what kind of support might be appropriate.

services.title: Forms of support
services.intro: The child, parent, and family relationships are considered together, in the context of development and experience. Explore the areas below or contact me if you are unsure what would be appropriate.
services.initial: During first contact, we clarify the request and discuss support appropriate to your circumstances.

items.title: Clinical psychological assessment
items.text: Assessment helps understand a child's or adolescent's emotional, behavioural, and relational functioning in the context of their development.
examples: Understanding the difficulties observed and the child's needs.
Clarifying possible directions for support and intervention.

items.title: Counselling for children and adolescents
items.text: Support adapted to a child's or adolescent's age and needs, in relation to everyday challenges.
examples: Changes in the family, at school, or in important relationships.

items.title: Integrative psychotherapy for children and adolescents
items.text: Relational integrative work considers the child within their story, development, and relationships. Goals and ways of working are developed collaboratively with the family.
examples: Understanding experiences and developing emotional resources.
Supporting relationships and more adaptive ways of meeting challenges.

items.title: Parent counselling
items.text: A space for reflection and support that considers the child's needs alongside the adult's resources, limits, and experiences.
examples: Understanding a child's behaviour and its context.

items.title: The parent–child relationship
items.text: Support to understand and improve the relationship between parent and child, with attention to each person's needs and perspective.
examples: Building more balanced ways of relating.

items.title: Family dynamics and relationships
items.text: We consider how relationships and changes within the family affect each member, without reducing difficulties to one person.
examples: Relationships between siblings and between children and caregivers.
Changes or tensions affecting the family's balance.

items.title: Online support for Romanians abroad
items.text: Psychological support sessions in Romanian, held exclusively online, for children, parents, and families living outside Romania.
examples: Suitability for online work is discussed individually.
Availability and arrangements are clarified before an appointment.

about.title: About me
about.valuesTitle: The values that guide my work

values.title: Relationship
values.text: Change begins and develops in safe, stable, authentic relationships.

values.title: Respect
values.text: I respect the pace, uniqueness, limits, and story of each person and family.

values.title: Professional ethics
values.text: I work responsibly, within clear professional boundaries, using scientifically grounded interventions.

values.title: Authenticity
values.text: I believe in a human, natural, sincere professional presence, without constructing an image of a ‘perfect’ professional.

values.title: Balance
values.text: I seek balance between emotion and reason, children's and parents' needs, acceptance and change, and professional and personal life.

resources.title: Resources for children, parents, and families
resources.intro: Perspectives and information to understand child development and family relationships. These materials are informative and do not replace an individual assessment or support.
resources.emptyText: Try another word or return to all topics.
resources.notice: General information does not establish a diagnosis or replace a discussion of your circumstances.

faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.intro: Answers that may help before first contact. You can send an inquiry about questions specific to your circumstances.

items.question: Do I need to know which service I need?
items.answer: No. You can choose ‘I'm not sure’ in the form. First contact helps clarify the request and discuss which direction of support may be appropriate.

items.question: Does submitting the form book an appointment?
items.answer: No. The form sends an inquiry. An appointment and working arrangements are agreed separately after discussing the request.

items.question: What should I include in the message?
items.answer: A brief message is enough, and the field is optional. For this first contact, avoid medical details and sensitive information about you or your child.

items.question: Are parents involved?
items.answer: Collaboration with parents is an important part of the process. Their involvement is adapted to the child's age, needs, and the goals agreed together.

items.question: How is the form of support chosen?
items.answer: The process begins with understanding the situation and clarifying needs. On this basis, we discuss goals and appropriate support within professional competencies.

items.question: How long does the work take?
items.answer: Duration varies with needs, goals, and progress. The website does not set a universal duration; arrangements and review of goals are discussed together.

items.question: Can I ask for support if I live outside Romania?
items.answer: You can ask about online support in Romanian. Suitability, whether working together is possible, and applicable arrangements are discussed individually before an appointment.

items.question: Are sessions available in every website language?
items.answer: The languages available on the website do not automatically indicate the languages in which sessions are provided. Please ask for clarification before an appointment.

items.question: How is confidentiality approached?
items.answer: Confidentiality and its limits are discussed within the working relationship, in line with applicable professional and legal obligations. It is not a promise without exceptions; you can ask about specific questions.

privacySections.title: First contact
privacySections.text: The form requests your name, email address, inquiry category, and an optional message. This information is used to receive and respond to your inquiry. Avoid medical details or other sensitive data in this first message.

privacySections.title: Sending an inquiry
privacySections.text: When the form is available, your inquiry is sent through EmailJS to the practice's contact address. You can also choose to email directly. Sending an inquiry does not confirm an appointment.

privacySections.title: Website hosting
privacySections.text: For the public website hosted on GitHub Pages, GitHub records visitor IP addresses for security purposes.

privacySections.title: Questions about your data
privacySections.text: For clarification about access to information, retention, or exercising applicable rights, you can email the contact address below.

cookieSections.title: Appearance preference
cookieSections.text: If you choose a light, dark, or system appearance, that choice may be stored locally in your browser. If storage is blocked, the website remains usable but your preference may not be remembered.

cookieSections.title: Page language
cookieSections.text: The language is determined by the page you visit. Changing language keeps the same page and, where relevant, the same section.

cookieSections.title: Analytics and advertising
cookieSections.text: This version of the website does not load traffic analytics or advertising tools. Form entries are not saved in the browser's local storage.
